title: Designing Monitoring and Logging
objective: Build an observable and protected monitoring foundation that correlates user impact, system state, and change history to enable detection.

sections.title: Choosing Metrics and Logs Based on Purpose
paragraphs: In observability design, distinguish request counts, latency, and error rates that show user impact from logs, traces, and resource metrics used to investigate causes. Define the namespace, dimensions, timestamps, owners, and retention period so that specific applications or environments can be compared later.

Logs and metrics have requirements for encryption at rest and in transit, write roles, viewing permissions, retention, and deletion. Increasing collection volume alone raises costs and makes searching more difficult, so choose the granularity and retention needed for the investigation purpose.

sources.label: DOP-C02 Exam Guide: Monitoring and Logging

sections.title: Connect alarms to actionable responses
paragraphs: CloudWatch alarms can evaluate a metric or mathematical expression against a threshold over an evaluation period, then send notifications or perform actions. Define more than just the alarm name: specify the operation being monitored, the rationale for the threshold, the evaluation period, how missing data is handled, the notification destination, and the response runbook.

An alarm does not prove the cause. Incident responders compare request volume, error rate, latency, deployments, configuration changes, and logs from dependencies during the same time period, then test the correlation as a hypothesis.

sections.title: Observability Across Complex Environments
paragraphs: In multi-account, multi-Region environments, determine where to aggregate logs, which dashboards each team will view, the shared correlation ID, access boundaries, and the evidence to retain during incidents. Do not make everything viewable through a single administrator permission; show each person only what they need for their duties.

Dashboards must provide more than status displays: after an anomaly is detected, they must provide paths to the affected resource, time, dependencies, and change history. Even if the display is green, do not exclude an issue from investigation when a user-impacting SLI has deteriorated.

sources.label: DOP-C02 Exam Guide: Monitoring Complex Environments

checkpoints.prompt: You are designing an observability platform to compare API quality across multiple products. Choose the one most appropriate metric design.

choices.text: Aggregate all metrics into a single value without dimensions.
choices.explanation: You cannot determine which product or operation had an impact.

choices.text: Store logs indefinitely without limits and grant everyone permission to view them.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirements for cost, searchability, or data protection.

choices.text: Define dimensions representing the application, environment, and operation, along with the request count, latency, and error rate, and also establish retention and access permissions.
choices.explanation: You can compare the impact on users for each target and protect the observability data.

checkpoints.prompt: A person designing an error-rate alarm for the order API wants to respond consistently after receiving a notification. Select the single most appropriate alarm configuration.

choices.text: Associate the alarm with the monitored operation, the basis for the threshold, the evaluation period, missing-data treatment, the notification target, and a runbook.
choices.explanation: This connects detection to a concrete response.

choices.text: Define only the alarm name, and leave the threshold and notification target to the person responsible.
choices.explanation: State transitions and responses will not be consistent.

choices.text: Assume the alarm is the cause and change every environment without verification.

checkpoints.prompt: We are investigating a production incident in a multi-account environment. Choose one most appropriate observability design.

choices.text: Copy the logs from all accounts to each responsible person’s device.
choices.explanation: This compromises evidence preservation and access controls.

choices.text: Look only at infrastructure metrics and do not collect metrics showing user impact.
choices.explanation: This makes it impossible to assess service quality.

choices.text: Design logs and dashboards that include correlation IDs, aggregation destinations, team-specific least-privilege access, and links to the change history.
choices.explanation: This enables cross-account investigation while maintaining access boundaries.
